# First read the setup file for functions as reading your google sheet database. 
```{r}
# include the setup file 
source(here::here("scripts","01-setup.R"))
```

# authenticate & read the Google sheets database
This now reads the Lauwersmeer data file from great tits

```{r}
gsheets_auth()  # you can put: email="c.both@rug.nl"


data<-read_gsdb("https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/10ftwcnis0hG8lLTPbWfEgOxTiErLVfSSDrt0hTB8ywE")

# This is needed for comments

str(data)
str(data$fact_biometry)
```

# select the data needed for the exercise
```{r}
# Convert nestbox_id to character
data$dim_nestboxes <- data$dim_nestboxes |>
  dplyr::mutate(nestbox_id = as.character(nestbox_id))

data$fact_biometry <- data$fact_biometry |>
  dplyr::mutate(nestbox_id = as.character(nestbox_id))

# Create data_F (female data)
data_F <- data$fact_biometry |>
  dplyr::left_join(data$dim_individuals, by = "individual_id") |>
  dplyr::filter(sex == 1) |> # select for females only
  dplyr::left_join(data$dim_years, by = "year") |>
  dplyr::left_join(data$dim_nestboxes, by = "nestbox_id") |>
  dplyr::select(-c(layingdate, wing, tarsus, weight,
                   fledglingnumber, recruit, survival, x_gps, y_gps)) # remove unecessary columns

str(data$fact_biometry)
str(data$dim_nestboxes)
```

# check for outliers
```{r}
#for example: 
hist(data_F$clutchsize)
```

# step 1: linear regression
 ```{r}
 m1<-lm(clutchsize~annual_density, data=data_F)
summary(m1)
```

# visualisation regression
```{r}
# Visualizing regression:
ggplot(data_F, aes(x=annual_density, y=clutchsize)) +
  geom_point(shape=1) +    # Use hollow circles
  geom_smooth(method=lm,   # Add linear regression line
              se=FALSE)+
  theme_classic(base_size = 15)
```
# check residuals
```{r}
# check residuals
plot(m1)
hist(residuals(m1))
```

# step 2. linear regression - density as factor
```{r}
data_F <- data_F |>
  dplyr::mutate(density_cat = as.factor(annual_density)) # create a new density variable that is treated as a factor


m2<-lm(clutchsize~density_cat, data=data_F)
summary(m2)
```

# step 3. linear regression - taking annual means
```{r}
#calculating mean clutch size + sd + se per density
data_means <- data_F |>
  dplyr::group_by(annual_density) |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    CS_avg = mean(clutchsize, na.rm = TRUE),
    CS_sd = sd(clutchsize, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_obs = sum(!is.na(clutchsize)),
    CS_se = CS_sd / sqrt(n_obs),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# using mean clutch size in the lm

m3<-lm(CS_avg~annual_density, data=data_means)
summary(m3)

# visualisation
ggplot(data_means, aes(x=annual_density, y=CS_avg)) + 
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=CS_avg-CS_se, ymax=CS_avg+CS_se), width=.1) +
  geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(method=lm,   # Add linear regression line
              se=FALSE)+
  theme_classic(base_size = 15)
```

# step 4 mixed models
```{r}

m4 <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
  clutchsize ~ +(1|individual_id), # individual_id is fitted as a random effect to account for repeated measurements within females
  family = gaussian(link = "identity"),
  data = data_F
)
m4
summary(m4)
confint(m4)

```

# calculating repeatability of clutch size based on m4

```{r}
# Extract variance components
var_components <- as.data.frame(glmmTMB::VarCorr(m4)$cond)
print(var_components)
names(var_components)

# Random effect variance
var_individual <- as.numeric(glmmTMB::VarCorr(m4)$cond$individual_id[1, 1])

# Residual variance
var_residual <- sigma(m4)^2

# Calculate repeatability
R_m4 <- var_individual / (var_individual + var_residual)
R_m4
```

# adding a fixed effect
```{r}
m5 <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
  clutchsize ~ annual_density +(1|individual_id), # individual_id is fitted as a random effect to account for repeated measurements within females
  family = gaussian(link = "identity"),
  data = data_F
)
m5
summary(m5)
confint(m5)

#calculating repeatability of clutch size based on m5

# Extract variance components
var_components <- as.data.frame(glmmTMB::VarCorr(m5)$cond)
print(var_components)
names(var_components)

# Random effect variance
var_individual <- as.numeric(glmmTMB::VarCorr(m5)$cond$individual_id[1, 1])

# Residual variance
var_residual <- sigma(m5)^2

# Calculate repeatability
R_m5 <- var_individual / (var_individual + var_residual)
R_m5
```
# adding a random effect
```{r}
m6 <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
  clutchsize ~ annual_density +(1|individual_id) + (1|plot_id), # individual_id is fitted as a random effect to account for repeated measurements within females, now we also add study areas
  family = gaussian(link = "identity"),
  data = data_F
)
m6
summary(m6)
confint(m6)

#calculating repeatability of clutch size based on m5

# Extract variance components
var_components <- as.data.frame(glmmTMB::VarCorr(m6)$cond)
print(var_components)
names(var_components)

# Random effect variance
var_individual <- as.numeric(glmmTMB::VarCorr(m6)$cond$individual_id[1, 1])

# Residual variance
var_residual <- sigma(m6)^2

# Calculate repeatability
R_m6 <- var_individual / (var_individual + var_residual)
R_m6
```

# step 5 within subject centering

```{r}

# Center annual density per individual
data_F <- data_F |>
  dplyr::group_by(individual_id) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    avgAnDens = mean(annual_density, na.rm = TRUE),
    annual_density_cen = annual_density - avgAnDens
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()


# Model with annual_density_cen (within-individual effect) and avgAnDens (between-individual effect)

m7 <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
  clutchsize ~ annual_density_cen + avgAnDens +
    (1 | individual_id) + (1 | plot_id),
  family = gaussian(link = "identity"),
  data = data_F
)

summary(m7)
confint(m7)
```
# visualisation

```{r}
library(viridis)

graph_m7 <- ggplot(data_F, aes(x = annual_density, y = clutchsize)) +
  geom_line(
    aes(group = individual_id, color = factor(individual_id)),
    alpha = 0.7, linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(color = factor(individual_id)),
    alpha = 0.8, size = 1
  ) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm", se = FALSE,
    color = "black", linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "turbo") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

graph_m7

  ```
